title: DF-Conformer: Integrated Architecture of Conv-TasNet and Conformer Using Linear Complexity Self-Attention for Speech Enhancement
venue: IEEE Workshop on Applications of Signal Processing to Audio and Acoustics (WASPAA)

citations.claim: Koizumi et al. proposed DF-Conformer, which integrates Conformer layers with dilated convolution layers from TDCN++ for single-channel speech enhancement, combining local and global sequential modeling.

DF-Conformer uses FAVOR+ (fast attention via positive orthogonal random features) to reduce the quadratic time complexity of multi-head self-attention to linear complexity, enabling the use of Conformer with short-hop trainable filterbanks.

DF-Conformer replaces the standard depthwise convolution in the Conformer block with stacked 1-D dilated depthwise convolutions, enabling a larger temporal receptive field without increasing model size.

In DF-Conformer, attention matrices in earlier layers tend to capture global noise characteristics across the full utterance, while deeper layers refine the mask using local structure, suggesting a coarse-to-fine processing hierarchy across layers.

The Conv-TasNet framework combines trainable analysis/synthesis filterbanks with a mask prediction network, where the encoder maps the time-domain signal to a representation, a mask is predicted, and the decoder reconstructs the enhanced signal.

Koizumi et al. demonstrated that combining dilated convolutions for local modeling with linear-complexity self-attention for global modeling achieves higher SI-SNR than using either mechanism alone for speech enhancement.

do_not_claim: DF-Conformer was applied to chromatogram baseline correction or chemical signal processing
DF-Conformer uses algorithm unrolling or deep unfolding
DF-Conformer eliminates the need for hyperparameter tuning
